title: The first television broadcast of the opening of parliament
text: The 22nd Canadian Parliament was in session from November 12, 1953, until April 12, 1957. The membership was set by the 1953 federal election on August 10, 1953, and it changed only somewhat due to resignations and by-elections until it was dissolved prior to the 1957 election.

title: The Bank of Toronto and The Dominion Bank merge to form the Toronto-Dominion Bank
text: The Bank of Toronto was a Canadian bank that was founded in 1855 by a group of grain dealers and flour millers. On February 1, 1955, it merged with the Dominion Bank to form the Toronto-Dominion Bank.

title: Military exercise Operation Bulldog III in Yellowknife.
text: Operation Bulldog III was a military exercise held in 1955 by the Canadian Army at Yellowknife, Northwest Territories, Canada.

title: The Angus L. Macdonald Bridge connecting Halifax to Dartmouth opens.
text: Dartmouth is a built-up community of the Halifax Regional Municipality, Nova Scotia, Canada. Located on the eastern shore of Halifax Harbour, Dartmouth has 72,139 residents as of 2021.

title: 1955 Ontario general election: Leslie Frost's PCs win a fourth consecutive majority
text: Leslie Miscampbell Frost was a politician in Ontario, Canada, who served as the province's 16th premier from May 4, 1949, to November 8, 1961. Due to his lengthy tenure, he gained the nickname "Old Man Ontario"; he was also known as "the Silver Fox".

title: 1955 Alberta general election: Ernest Manning's Social Credit Party wins a sixth consecutive majority.
text: Ernest Charles Manning was a Canadian politician and the eighth premier of Alberta between 1943 and 1968 for the Social Credit Party of Alberta. He served for 25 years, longer than any other premier in the province's history and the second longest-serving provincial premier in Canadian history (after George Henry Murray of Nova Scotia).

title: Cape Breton Island is connected to the mainland by the Canso Causeway
text: Cape Breton Island is a rugged and irregularly shaped island on the Atlantic coast of North America, forming part of the Canadian province of Nova Scotia. The 10,513.1 km2 island accounts for 18.7% of Nova Scotia's total area.
